key_insight: Crystal structural prototypes provide a unifying framework for grouping materials by recurring atomic arrangements, but the result depends strongly on how structure equivalence is defined and how neighbors are assigned.
engineering_relevance: Prototype libraries enable high-throughput materials discovery, structure prediction, and generative design by allowing chemical substitution, derivative enumeration, and template-based candidate generation.
method: Surveyed prototype construction methods spanning crystallographic curation, standardization, geometric matching, local-environment clustering, and periodic-graph analysis.
Compared major prototype libraries and structure-type databases, including AFLOW, CSPD, LAE-ICSPD, EMFDTW, TYPIX, and ICSD structure types.
Evaluated GraphID-based family assignment and benchmarked generative CSP models using template retrieval and stoichiometry-held-out tests.
evidence_signal: Across ICSD, Materials Project, OQMD, and LeMat samples, the 100 most frequent families covered 30–67% of structures, 72–82% of families were singletons, and up to 76% of GraphIDs changed when neighbor tolerance varied.
watch_item: Prototype assignments can be highly sensitive to neighbor-definition choices and stoichiometric coverage, so reported performance may reflect library bias rather than true generalization to unseen structures.
paper_title: A Comprehensive Survey of Crystal Structural Prototypes: Construction, Classification, and Applications
